source_snapshot.items: Test connections between HMC I2C-13, BMC I2C-16 and UPHY3 from second PG548
source_snapshot.procedure: From BMC run broad `i2cdetect -y -q 15` and `i2ctransfer -y 15 w3@0x44 0xc0 0x0 0x0 r4`; PID1114953.
source_snapshot.criteria: Collect evidence/photos and check logs; no path ownership or four-byte oracle.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO; replaces the remote BMC transaction with probing/soldering.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: Flags mapping/write risk but omits dual-controller arbitration and keeps physical inspection primary.

old_problem: BMC I2C-16/HMC I2C-13-to-bus15 topology, multi-master/bridge/mux ownership,0x44 second-PG548 UPHY3 identity,0xc00000 semantics, four-byte decoder, scan policy and recovery are absent.
disposition_reason: The BMC-side combined read can be a functional test, but the row names two management controllers and therefore requires authoritative path ownership/arbitration before raw access. ED-03 forbids guessing the UPHY register/response; an ACK cannot prove second-PG548 UPHY3 or both controller segments.
decision_basis: Read XLSX row135, same-row AI fields and history2524; unique identity confirmed.
Preserved HMC I2C-13, BMC I2C-16, bus15,0x44,0xc00000,r4 and second-PG548 UPHY3.
Made shared-bus arbitration, peer quiescence and ownership restoration explicit.
Rejected broad quick-write scan and invented probing; no bus access, retry, reset or DUT action occurred.

test_case.test_name: Dual-controller bus15 to second-PG548 UPHY3 functional read
test_case.purpose: Verify the BMC I2C-16/HMC I2C-13 management path reaches UPHY3 on the second PG548 using one decoded read without controller contention.
required_package: Current owner and approved arbitration/quiescence/restoration procedure
UPHY0xc00000 non-mutating 24-bit pointer semantics and four-byte decoder
Timeout/NACK/arbitration criteria and independent BMC/HMC recovery
test_case.test_command: Do not run broad `i2cdetect -q`. After topology, ownership and register approval, capture BMC/HMC/UPHY identities and error state; quiesce or arbitrate the peer; execute one `i2ctransfer -y 15 w3@0x44 0xc0 0x0 0x0 r4`; decode all fields, restore ownership and verify both controllers without retry.
test_case.expected_result: The exact request returns four bytes matching the signed UPHY3 oracle, no collision or new BMC/HMC/UPHY error occurs, ownership is restored, and both management paths remain healthy.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires controller/path ownership proof, exact UPHY3 identity, decoded expected fields and successful restoration. ACK/raw bytes, wrong target/value/length, arbitration loss, NACK/timeout/stuck bus, restoration failure or new error fails.
safety_gate: Prove current bus owner and coordinate/quiesce the peer controller.
Confirm0xc00000 is a non-mutating read pointer for this UPHY revision.
No broad quick-write scan or forced concurrent access.
One bounded transfer; stop on first contention/error, preserve evidence and do not retry/reset.
expected_evidence: PID dual-controller topology and current ownership
Timestamped transfer, raw/decoded bytes, exit status and latency
Arbitration state, pre/post errors, ownership restoration, endpoint health and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Restore only the approved mux/ownership state. On contention or health loss, preserve evidence and use the independently approved BMC/HMC recovery path; no automatic retry or controller reset.

source_conflict.reason: Two logical controllers are named but topology/ownership, UPHY identity and response oracle are omitted; earlier reviews add unsourced physical work.

blocked.reason: The bounded functional operation is known; OEM topology, decoder and arbitration are supplyable RPUC prerequisites.
